candidate.title: PAL-seq
candidate.scope: The middle PAL-seq row of the supplied Illumina poster crop: the original splinted-adapter, bead-capture and fluorescence-based poly(A)-tail profiling architecture described by Subtelny et al. (2014). The neighboring TAIL-seq and FRT-Seq rows, cropped RARseq material above, and chemical structures at right are catalogue context, not alternatives within this card. The verified PAL-Seq collection page is secondary clarification of the same target. Its mention of 3P-Seq describes a shared preparation component, not another target method. No unshown adaptation or complete laboratory implementation is asserted.

states.label: Cluster fluorescence paired with identifying sequence
features: The final bright-spot scan is an optical measurement of tail-associated labeling at each cluster.

The primary paper interprets cluster-density-normalized, standard-calibrated fluorescence as a tail-length estimate paired with its identifying sequence, called a poly(A) tag; raw spot intensity alone is not an absolute length.

The assay measures retained RNA tail lengths, not translation itself. Selection of compatible polyadenylated ends limits the represented population; the secondary catalogue flags adenine-only end capture and possible extension-efficiency effects.

operations.label: Ligate splint oligo
operations.description: Join the RNA poly(A) 3′ end to a biotinylated DNA adapter using the separate splint oligonucleotide. The product acquires an adapter interface and a capture handle. The caption is preserved, with its chemical meaning resolved from the primary paper.
operations.mechanism: Splinted ligation; the primary implementation uses T4 RNA ligase 2. The adapter is covalently attached. The separate T-rich splint is a noncovalent alignment reagent, represented here as a component rather than as material consumed to form the library.
operations.information_effect: Retains each captured native tail attached to its RNA-body sequence and adds a biotin-mediated capture interface. Compatibility with the splinted ligation is a selection, not proof that every biological RNA species is recovered.
